exposure: Prenatal selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) treatment
cohort: 845,345 singleton live births in Finland between 1996 and 2010
finding: Prenatal SSRI treatment was associated with a lower risk of preterm birth and cesarean section but a higher risk of neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Offspring of mothers who received SSRIs during pregnancy had a lower risk of cesarean section compared with offspring of mothers unexposed to medications but with psychiatric disorders (odds ratio=0.70, 95% CI=0.66-0.75).
